import math
# Logistic regression, gradient descent, standard library only.
weights = [0.0] * len(X_train[0]); bias = 0.0; lr = 0.1
for epoch in range(300):
    grad_w = [0.0] * len(weights); grad_b = 0.0
    for xi, yi in zip(X_train, y_train):
        z = sum(w * v for w, v in zip(weights, xi)) + bias
        p = 1 / (1 + math.exp(-z))
        err = p - yi
        for j, v in enumerate(xi):
            grad_w[j] += err * v
        grad_b += err
    n = len(X_train)
    weights = [w - lr * g / n for w, g in zip(weights, grad_w)]
    bias -= lr * grad_b / n
def predict(x):
    return 1 if sum(w * v for w, v in zip(weights, x)) + bias > 0 else 0
model = {"weights": weights, "bias": bias, "predict": predict}
print("weights", [round(w, 3) for w in weights], "bias", round(bias, 3))
description: Logistic regression by plain gradient descent in pure Python (no numpy needed). Defines `model` = {weights, bias, predict}.
